title: What Rats Know About Social Signals

paragraphs.english: Rats and other animals need to be highly attuned to social signals from others so they can identify friends to cooperate with and enemies to avoid.To find out if this extends to non-living beings, Laleh Quinn at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues tested whether rats can detect social signals from robotic rats.
paragraphs.chinese: 大鼠和其他动物需要对同类发出的社交信号高度敏感，以便识别可以合作的朋友和需要躲避的敌人。为了弄清这种能力是否也适用于非生物，加利福尼亚大学圣迭戈分校的拉莱·奎因及其同事，测试了大鼠能否识别机器鼠发出的社交信号。

paragraphs.english: They housed eight adult rats with two types of robotic rat—one social and one asocial—for four days.The robot rats were quite minimalist, resembling a chunkier version of a computer mouse with wheels-to move around and colorful markings.
paragraphs.chinese: 他们让八只成年大鼠与两类机器鼠共同生活四天，一类具有社交性，另一类不具有社交性。这些机器鼠的设计相当简约，像加厚版的电脑鼠标，装有用于移动的轮子和一些彩色标记。

paragraphs.english: During the experiment, the social robot rat followed the living rats around, played with the same toys, and opened cage doors to let trapped rats escape. Meanwhile, the asocial robot simply moved forwards and backwards and side to side.
paragraphs.chinese: 实验过程中，具有社交性的机器鼠跟着真正的大鼠四处活动，玩相同的玩具，还会打开笼门，让被困的大鼠逃出去。与此同时，不具有社交性的机器鼠，只是前后左右来回移动。

paragraphs.english: Next, the researchers trapped the robots in cages and gave the rats the opportunity to release them by pressing a lever.Across 18 trials each, the living rats were 52 per cent more likely on average to set the social robot free than the asocial one. This suggests that the rats perceived the social robot as a genuine social being, says Quinn. The rats may have bonded more with the social robot because it displayed behaviors like communal exploring and playing. This could lead to the rats better remembering having freed it earlier, and wanting the robot to return the favour when they get trapped, she says .
paragraphs.chinese: 接下来，研究者把机器鼠困在笼子里，让真正的大鼠有机会通过按压杠杆将其释放。每只大鼠都接受了十八次测试，平均而言，释放具有社交性的机器鼠的可能性，比释放另一类机器鼠高出百分之五十二。奎因说，这表明大鼠把具有社交性的机器鼠当作真正的社会性个体。大鼠可能与它建立了更强的联结，因为它表现出了共同探索和玩耍等行为。她说，这或许使大鼠更容易记住自己先前释放过它，并希望当自己被困时，机器鼠也能回报。

paragraphs.english: “Rats have been shown to engage in multiple forms of reciprocal help and cooperation, including what is referred to as direct reciprocity where a rat will help another rat that has previously helped them,” says Quinn.
paragraphs.chinese: 奎因说：“已经有研究表明，大鼠会进行多种形式的互助与合作，包括所谓的直接互惠，也就是一只大鼠会帮助此前曾帮助过自己的另一只大鼠。”

paragraphs.english: The readiness of the rats to befriend the social robot was surprising given its minimal design.The robot was the same size as a regular rat but resembled a simple plastic box on wheels. “ We’d assumed we’d have to give it a moving head and tail, facial features, and put a scent on it to make it smell like a real rat, but that wasn’t necessary, ” says Janet Wiles at the University of Queensland in Australia, who helped with the research.
paragraphs.chinese: 考虑到机器鼠的设计如此简单，大鼠竟然乐意与这只社交型机器鼠交朋友，着实令人惊讶。它和普通大鼠一样大，看上去却只是一个装在轮子上的简单塑料盒。参与研究的澳大利亚昆士兰大学研究者珍妮特·怀尔斯说：“我们原以为，得给它加上会动的头和尾巴、面部特征，再涂上气味，让它闻起来像真正的大鼠，但事实证明没有必要。”

paragraphs.english: The finding shows how sensitive rats are to social cues, even when they come from basic robots. says Wiles. Similarly, children tend to treat robots as if they are fellow beings, even when they display only simple social signals. “We humans seem to be fascinated by robots, and it turns out other animals are too,” says Wiles.
paragraphs.chinese: 怀尔斯说，这一发现表明，大鼠对社交线索非常敏感，哪怕线索来自结构简单的机器人。类似地，即使机器人只表现出简单的社交信号，儿童也倾向于把它们当成同伴。怀尔斯说：“我们人类似乎对机器人十分着迷，结果发现，其他动物也是如此。”

sentenceNotes.sentence: “Rats have been shown to engage in multiple forms of reciprocal help and cooperation, including what is referred to as direct reciprocity where a rat will help another rat that has previously helped them,” says Quinn.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: Rats have been shown to engage in multiple forms of reciprocal help and cooperation.
sentenceNotes.structure: have been shown 为现在完成时被动语态；including 后 what 从句表示“被称为直接互惠的行为”；where 从句解释这种行为的情境；that 从句修饰 another rat。
sentenceNotes.translation: 奎因说，研究已表明，大鼠会进行多种互助与合作，包括所谓的直接互惠：一只大鼠帮助此前帮助过自己的另一只大鼠。
sentenceNotes.tip: where 在此引出某种互惠情境，不能机械译为地点“哪里”。

sentenceNotes.sentence: “ We’d assumed we’d have to give it a moving head and tail, facial features, and put a scent on it to make it smell like a real rat, but that wasn’t necessary, ” says Janet Wiles at the University of Queensland in Australia, who helped with the research.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: We had assumed we would have to add features and scent, but that wasn’t necessary.
sentenceNotes.structure: 第一个 We’d 为 had，第二个 we’d 为 would；assumed 后省略 that；give 与 put 为并列动作；to make ... 表示目的；who 从句修饰发言人 Janet Wiles。
sentenceNotes.translation: 参与研究的昆士兰大学研究者怀尔斯说：“我们原以为，得给它装上会动的头尾、面部特征，并加上气味，使它闻起来像真正的大鼠，但这些都没有必要。”
sentenceNotes.tip: 同样缩写 ’d 可分别代表 had 与 would，要根据 assumed 和 have to 的结构判断。
